definition: The process of establishing consistent processes, formats, or configurations across an organization to improve efficiency and reduce complexity.
extendedDefinition: Standardization is the practice of establishing consistent processes, formats, and configurations across an organization to reduce complexity and improve efficiency. In software terms, it covers everything from naming conventions and data structures to approved tool lists and security configurations. Standardization lowers administrative overhead, simplifies training, and makes reporting comparable across teams, since everyone operates against the same definitions. It also reduces vendor sprawl: fewer platforms and consistent integrations cut cost and consolidate purchasing leverage. The risk is over-standardization, where rigid rules ignore legitimate variation and force teams into mismatched workflows. Effective standardization is negotiated with stakeholders, documented, and reviewed as needs evolve. Buyers should consider how well a product supports standard templates, permission models, and configurations, since these enforce consistency without eliminating flexibility.
